## Hunt for Additional Indicators

Take action on the analysis above.

First, check if `dream-me[.]com` is used maliciously. You can't tell via urlscan. The Dynamic Delivery Domains will only be requested when the user clicks the download button, so the urlscan scans won't have the HTTP transactions for them. You'll need to check via Any Run submissions. Go to https://app.any.run/submissions, and search for the domain. I will use the session linked below.

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

https://app.any.run/tasks/ef4675d6-9792-4a27-adfa-c3be244ddcde

We've found a WinSCP-themed lure delivering Oyster - `winscp[.]id`.

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Perform a cursory glance.

## Validate winscp[.]id

Check `winscp[.]id` in urlscan.

https://urlscan.io/search/#winscp.id

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

https://urlscan.io/result/01992f06-6e3a-764c-983f-f4e2a7a839c7/

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Observe the `download12.js` file: https://urlscan.io/responses/0b58a544d5e0323bd910dceebe311ab1c1df098c63b4bfca0399a9d83dd762f6/

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

It contains the following Dynamic Delivery Domains (apiUrls):

```
dream-me[.]com
msaonl[.]com
ncvalor[.]com
newfrontieradvisorsllc[.]com
newhampshirehomebuyer[.]com
```

Success!

We will have to add the new indicators to the Indicator Table after we include this section as a source in the Source Table.

## Analyze dream-me[.]com

Now that we've validated `dream-me[.]com` is used maliciously, we can thruntellisearch on the previously identified patterns.

`page.title:"dream-me.com"`
https://urlscan.io/search/#page.title%3A%22dream-me.com%22

Note that the top result was 8 hours ago at the time of creating this content. 

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Recall that you need to search these domains in Any Run to seem them used. Search Any Run for the `doctorreportcard[.]com` indicator.

https://app.any.run/tasks/cf7fdd9a-8d74-4308-8923-2c5c525ded38

**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Observe the Any Run session is from a different lure - Notepad++ (`notepad-plus-plus[.]run`). Keep in mind that many different lure pages can use the same Dynamic Delivery Domain. Because of that, it is possible to find additional lures - just like we have - by searching for the domain in Any Run. We can take the domain from the session and add that to the indicator table.

With this final check, we will add the visible domains from the urlscan pivot, and the newly observed Notepad++ lure - `notepad-plus-plus[.]run`. Note that you should add all indicators, not just the visible ones. Also note that you should continue searching for each Dynamic Delivery Domain in Any Run to identify additional lure themes. For the sake of brevity, I will be limiting it. The point is for you to learn the concepts.

## Summary

We've analyzed the Dynamic Delivery Domains. These domains are stored in the `apiUrls` array of the `download*.js` file. You don't generate a request to one of the domains by accessing the lure page - you have to click the download button to generate a request to the Dynamic Delivery Domain. Because of that, you need to search for the domain in Any Run. We've identified a WinSCP lure and a Notepad++ lure that could lead us to additional adversary infrastructure (in a future section).
